questions.prompt: Why is the number of contacts not enough to measure support?
questions.answer: Availability, quality and fit with the need matter.
questions.feedback: Give an example of a mismatch.

questions.answer: A proposed pattern in which support moderates the adverse relationship between stress and well-being.
questions.feedback: Do not claim every interaction buffers stress.

questions.answer: It is specific, bounded, voluntary and allows refusal.

questions.prompt: Can peer support replace professional assessment?
questions.answer: No; it can complement qualified care and help with access.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Matches support types to needs and drafts consent-based requests, alternatives and role boundaries.
scoring.transfer: Create a fictional support network map with four support types, a specific request for two and an alternative for each. Explain how consent and the helper's capacity change the plan. No names or personal contact information are needed.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
